summary:
The draft of lane work-04 is sound after repairs, and both recommendations stay. Skills loaded: ariakit-general-workflow and ariakit-general-code-style (remote github.com/ariakit/visonaut; no skill for this repository exists). The repository is unchanged (the same git status as at the start).

What I checked:
- I read the code lines behind each fact: the key handler, the viewer panes, the save path, the review service, the copy rule, and the lab menus. All held.
- I ran the first agent's probe again at both sizes. Each statement and row count is the same: 2,091 rows today against 1,251 for one run command at 246 changes, 18 statements at 246 and at 3,832 targets, and 8 rows in the service call for the one-row write.
- I fetched the three Cloudflare pages again on 2026-10-06. The quotes are exact.

One real gap in the draft: it said that a rejected variant stays as it is. That is true only inside one run. In my new probe, reviewer B rejected variant r3 in run 1 of a pull request. Run 2 had the same pixels, r3 had no decision, and the API answer had no sign of the Reject. A run approval in run 2 approved r3, and the run passed. This is also the behavior of A and Shift+A today, and the selected D-OPS-06 rule does not change it. A rule that leaves such a variant out worked in the probe as one more read condition (18 statements, no row written for r3). The section, the option text, and the rationale now say this and ask the maintainer whether he wants the rule.

The new probe also settled four points in favor of the recommended design:
- A later run copies the approvals of a run approval with no code change.
- Reject, Undo, run approval, Undo, and a second run approval give no revision conflict.
- Undo of a run approval is refused, and writes nothing, after another reviewer rejects one target.
- A second run approval at the same run revision is refused and writes nothing.

Other repairs: the Worker sets its subrequest limit to 250,000, which the draft did not say; the page and Undo each need a new branch; the guards protect against a mistake and not against intent; D02, D21, and P02 now have their meaning in words; and the consequences of the recommended option are shorter.

recommendations.reason: It is what the maintainer's note asks for, and it passes the three standing rules. D1 writes do not increase: the check passes only when each change has an approval, so the 246 decision rows are written in any case, and one command removes 40 x 21 fixed rows (1,251 against 2,091, measured twice on local D1). It needs 18 statements and a command row of about 390 characters at 246 and at 3,832 targets, where one list of all targets passes the documented 2 MB row limit at about 3,690. It keeps ordinary decision rows, so no code that reads decisions changes. The checker cases confirm the behavior: a later run copies the approvals, a stale run revision and a wrong count write nothing, and Undo is refused after another decision on a target. The one-row option saves about 2 US cents for the largest run and puts a second meaning of 'approved' in 11 source files, also in history.ts:173, which deletes comparison rows that have no decision row.
recommendations.wrongIf: Production D1 refuses or counts the two set-based statements in another way than local D1 (not measured; statements of the same form already run for each comparison in local-comparison.ts:612-626). Or the maintainer wants the fewest D1 writes more than one meaning of 'approved' (then approve-run-one-row). Or the maintainer does not accept that a run approval can approve changes that nobody opened, and pixels that a reviewer rejected one push before (then keep-scope, seen-set, or approve-run with the extra rule of case 5). Or a path exists where the page counts a change as 'needs review' and the server query does not: the count guard then refuses each run approval of that run.

recommendations.reason: The maintainer selected it. The code confirms his note: F sets the view 'new', G sets 'original', both images stay in the page, and the verifier measured the same rectangle for both, so F, then G, is the blink. The final modes have one key each: F current (first view, mask on), G baseline, D mask off and on, S two panes, W swipe, O overlay. Only W and O are new. A search of every key handler in apps/web/src found no meaning for W or O today, and the lab designs and map C of the audit use these letters. The option adds reads only, no D1 write.
recommendations.wrongIf: The maintainer wants other letters than W and O. Or the wait for the mask request in production is long (not measured). Or the maintainer wants the blink with F and G to work with no press of D first: with the mask on at load, the red pixels cover the change.

remainingDoubts: No number of this lane comes from production. All D1 numbers are from local D1 (Miniflare) with the repository code and synthetic rows of production length. Nobody compared the local rows_written with a production bill.

How D1 counts a batch toward 'Queries per Worker invocation: 1000' is still not known. The Worker sets subrequests to 250,000, which suggests that the limit is not at 1,000, but no page says that the two numbers are the same limit. The recommended design does not depend on it; the list design and the group option do.
The page parts of the run approval are text only: the menu item, the confirmation, and the count of opened changes. The readers of the one-row option are a design on paper.

The rule that keeps out a change whose pixels were rejected in an earlier run is a prototype of one SQL condition. It was tested with 4 rows. Its read cost for a run with 3,832 variants is not measured, and the page would need the same count as the server.

The prototype defines 'no decision' as decision_id IS NULL AND source_decision_id IS NULL. The page uses 'no decision in force'. I found no path in the code where they differ. If one exists, the run approval is refused; it does not approve a wrong variant.

The Undo of a run approval works only in the same tab, before a reload, and before another decision on one of its targets (as each Undo today). After that, the way back is Reject, one screenshot at a time. The maintainer has not said whether that is acceptable for a run approval.

Whether the confirmation stays is the maintainer's choice. He selected 'no dialog, visible Undo' for the whole screenshot (D-WORK-06). The recommended option keeps a confirmation and says how to drop it.

For the coordinator: D-WORK-02 stays 'open' in the patch, although the maintainer selected the option, because the letters W and O are new to him. notes.md has proposed settledAnswer and rationale text if the coordinator settles it.
For the coordinator: the demo and the text of D-WORK-03 still name a blink key (map C, 'T, held'). They belong to that decision and its unselected option, so this lane did not change them.

Design 2 (one list) at 3,832 targets through the route left the queue task in the state 'leased' with no result in both runs of the probe. Both ran on one busy computer, so it is not in the record, but it needs a measurement before anyone builds that design.
